ArXiv cs.AI.title: Alignment Faking Depends on the Value, Not Just the Model
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03650v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models can follow a directive when they believe they are monitored and abandon it when they believe they are not, a pattern termed Alignment Faking. Prior work establishes this for harmful-content objectives and a handful of moral-foundations values, leaving open how it distributes across a wider value space. We argue it is value-dependent: whether compliance survives a change in perceived oversight is a property of the model--value pairing, not of the model alone. Our framework profiles Alignment Faking per value, scoring each model-va

ArXiv cs.AI.title: CARD: A Proof-Carrying Certificate-to-Action Interface for Relative-Measurement Graphs
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03651v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Geometric certificates make mathematical claims about specified estimator objects, while robotic action requires a physical transform, a service decision, and timely proof support. We present CARD, a proof-carrying interface that keeps these objects distinct and records how they combine. Its lifted-fiber formulation separates semantic motion from witness repair and characterizes when projected and proof-carrying costs coincide. Its actionability result gives an exact useful-service law: uniform sampling without replacement produces a hypergeomet

ArXiv cs.AI.title: MCPGuard: Finding Conformance Gaps in MCP SDKs via Dual-Track Analysis and Dynamic Adjudication
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03662v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects large language model agents to external tools and services through official SDKs that implement message validation and session logic. Specification constraints omitted by these SDKs may propagate to downstream applications, highlighting the importance of SDK-level conformance testing. Yet existing MCP conformance tools mainly exercise running endpoints and reveal little about whether SDK models enforce specification requirements. We present MCPGuard, an automated LLM-based framework for detecting specifi

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03684v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models serve as the reasoning core of agents for chemistry and materials science, where they must interpret molecular structure before planning syntheses or proposing materials. Yet their outputs show only what they say, not what they know. Given a prompt such as ``The primary functional group in 1-Fluorobutane (CCCCF) is'', a small general-purpose model may answer ``the alkyne group'' instead of an alkyl fluoride. The output alone cannot tell whether the model failed to recognize the fluorine or recognized it and failed to say so. We a

ArXiv cs.AI.title: LOLPlay: Benchmarking Real-Time Visual Agents in League of Legends
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03685v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual agents need to coordinate reasoning and action while their environment evolves during inference. We introduce LOLPlay, a benchmark in native \emph{League of Legends} with 36 champion-specific tasks spanning resource management, combat, cooperation, and objectives. Agents interact through screenshots and mouse--keyboard actions; automated initialization and 82 executable subgoal checks distinguish partial progress from completion. Across 324 task evaluations of three models at three reasoning-effort settings, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highe

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Training LLM Agents to Automate LLM Post-Training with RSI-Dojo
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03698v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) aims to enable AI systems to autonomously build and improve AI systems themselves, including models, harnesses, and underlying infrastructure. Within this broader agenda, a central capability is enabling agents to train and improve base models. However, existing studies on automated model training primarily focused on workflow- or harness-level optimizations, rather than internalizing the ability to conduct post-training into the model itself. Developing this capability requires executable model training environm

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Unsatz: Evaluating Scientific Discovery Without a Given Ansatz
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03713v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Before a scientist fits any parameter, they must decide what the model contains: which quantities exist, which are hidden, how they interact, and how they are measured. Physicists call such a trial form an ansatz. Benchmarks for automated equation discovery mostly supply it, by fixing the variables, a library of candidate terms, or a law to be modified. We introduce Unsatz, a benchmark in which an LLM agent must construct the ansatz itself. Each task is a simulated system, generated from a private seed as a program in a small modeling language:

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03721v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in artificial-intelligence-assisted mathematics show that open-ended machine search can outperform human mathematicians, yet transferring this paradigm to physics requires refactoring the research workflow. We introduce Simjecture, an open-source framework in which language-model agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures. The framework tackles two central challenges in this transfer: first, because physics is empirical and no model is final, it structures inquiry around counterexample-driven falsification and prospect

ArXiv cs.AI.title: EMBERS: Empirically Motivated Robustness Testing of Deep Research Systems via Defect-Guided Fuzzing
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03723v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep Research (DR) systems extend large language models into autonomous agents that decompose complex information needs, iteratively search the web, and synthesize evidence to answer challenging questions. However, their multi-stage execution may introduce robustness risks, as variations in user questions or intermediate search inputs may propagate across research stages and lead to incorrect answers. Existing evaluations focus on task-solving capabilities or robustness against external evidence disturbances, leaving intrinsic weaknesses in DR e

ArXiv cs.AI.title: From Logs to Faults: Reference-Free Fault Localization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipelines
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03725v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines are widely used for domain-specific question answering, yet locating faults remains manual and time-consuming. Fault localization is challenging because RAG pipelines consist of interdependent stages, where faults can propagate downstream, masking their origin, or remain undetected even when the final answer is correct. Existing evaluation approaches often focus on individual stages and rely on reference answers or code instrumentation. We present RAGLog, which detects and localizes faults across RA

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Reasoning is topologically simple
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We formulate and investigate the hypothesis that reasoning text has simpler co-occurrence topology than non-reasoning text, and that higher-quality reasoning has simpler co-occurrence topology than lower-quality reasoning. We discuss and test applications to AI safety and AI evaluation.

ArXiv cs.AI.title: VagueBench: Benchmarking the Robustness of Embodied Agents on Ambient Context Illusions
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03765v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Embodied agents are increasingly deployed in open-world environments, yet current robustness evaluations remain biased toward hazardous instructions and jailbreak vulnerabilities. A more fundamental issue is largely overlooked: agents are rarely tested under semantically sufficient but contextually minimal instructions (i.e., common in real-world human communication), where auxiliary contextual cues are absent. For the first, we identify a novel phenomenon termed Ambient Context Illusion, where agents fail to execute tasks correctly when non-ess

ArXiv cs.AI.title: El Agente F\'armaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03832v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational drug discovery offers a growing range of tools for proposing and evaluating molecules, but combining them and deciding what to do next still requires substantial expert effort. Here, we introduce El Agente F\'armaco, an AI scientist that uses modern large language model (LLM) technology to turn discovery goals expressed in everyday language into complex, scalable computational screening workflows. The agentic harness selects scientific tools, reviews their results, and adjusts subsequent steps to the target and the user's objective

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging for Efficient Long-to-Short Reasoning
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03834v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-to-Short (L2S) model merging seeks to combine the strong reasoning capability of long chain-of-thought models with the concise style of base models, but existing methods that rely on linear interpolation and first-order activation statistics fail to capture how the loss landscape responds to parameter displacement, leading to degraded accuracy on hard tasks. We propose Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging (LHM), a training-free framework that replaces heuristic statistics with lightweight second-order curvature information. LHM consists of three c

ArXiv cs.AI.title: LaplaceDiag: Fault Diagnosis through Changes in Learned Actuator Effects
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.03849v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Identifying faulty components from sensor anomalies is difficult because fault effects can propagate through a plant and different faults can produce similar observations. Detailed component models and labeled fault examples may also be unavailable. We introduce LaplaceDiag, a data-driven method that uses changes in actuator effects to narrow the search for faulty equipment. Actuators act on specific devices and mechanisms, so their changed effects can provide clues to root causes. LaplaceDiag learns a healthy plant model with LaplaceNet, a neur

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Latent Cluster Separation as a Regularizer for Lifelong Anomaly Detection
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Lifelong (continual) anomaly detection systems must learn a sequence of tasks without forgetting how to recognize anomaly types seen earlier -- a property known as backward transfer. A common way to try to improve backward transfer is to reshape a model's internal representation around learnable concept centroids, typically coupled with a new way of scoring anomalies based on distance to those centroids. Because these two design choices are usually introduced together, it is unclear which one is actually responsible for any performance gain. In

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Four Extensions of the Universal Law of Robustness: Log-Concave Covariates, Heterogeneous Mixtures, Vector-Valued Predictors, and Markovian Data
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03653v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Bubeck and Sellke's universal law of robustness says that fitting $n$ noisy samples below the noise level with a class of $p$ real parameters forces a Lipschitz constant of order $\sqrt{nd/p}$, when the covariate distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isoperimetric: smooth interpolation costs a factor $d$ of overparametrization. Its hypotheses are Gaussian-type concentration, a homogeneous covariate law, scalar outputs, and independent samples; we relax each one. Exponential concentration suffices, at the unchanged rate and absolute constant and at t

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Towards Automatic Heart Murmur Characterization from Multi-spot Phonocardiograms
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03654v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cardiac auscultation traditionally detects the presence of a heart murmur, but clinicians further characterize it by timing, shape, pitch, quality, and grade. Most automatic phonocardiogram analysis systems stop at binary detection and do not estimate this richer description. In this work, we formulate automatic murmur characterization as five patient-level classification tasks and compare three multi-spot strategies on recordings from the aortic, pulmonary, mitral, and tricuspid auscultation locations. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Mixture of Wide Experts: Sparse Routing for Interpretable Native Coordinates
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03655v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models often spread a concept across many internal dimensions, making their features difficult to interpret. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) recover clearer features after training. We ask whether models can instead learn interpretable output coordinates directly. We introduce Mixture of Wide Experts (MoWE), a sparse feed-forward layer in which selected experts read the full representation but write to fixed, disjoint output coordinates. On a controlled task with known hidden causes, this design preserves predictive performance while localiz

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Stress-Testing the Robustness of LLM-Based Causal Inference
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03656v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Why do some of the world's most powerful Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems still struggle to reason about cause and effect? Causal discovery, the ability to discern the underlying drivers of a system, is fundamental to scientific inquiry and has traditionally relied on structured data and statistical methods. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been explored as an alternative paradigm for causal inference, leveraging their broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities. Yet, despite their linguistic fluency, LLMs often rely on surface-lev

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03675v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep neural networks extract powerful latent representations from images, enabling fast and efficient downstream analysis. However, these latent spaces lack explicit geometric structure, leading to possibly poor interpolation fidelity and misleading extrapolation. Latent interpolation techniques assume symmetric transition costs which are often not the case for real world data. Their symmetric nature cannot capture directional processes, such as disease progression, where certain transitions are impossible (e.g. tumor growth dynamics or cognitiv

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Does the Trust Boundary Hold over Time? A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Receiver-Directed Federated Learning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03724v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In receiver-directed federated learning, each site draws a trust boundary. For every source and model component it judges, on its own data, whether the transfer helps (admit), harms (reject) or cannot yet be told (abstain). We ask whether this boundary holds over hundreds of rounds. Our benchmark has a federation of thirteen semi-synthetic sites, an exact oracle for every evaluated transfer, paired seeds, an attack protocol, fourteen methods over 600 rounds and Qwen3-1.7B LoRA sites over 500. The answer depends on which boundary is measured. Acr

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Auditing a Model-Hub Benchmark: Data Quality, Training Budgets, and Side Information in HuggingBench
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03727v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Benchmarks built from model hubs combine interaction data, knowledge graphs (KGs) and resource documentation, but valid files do not ensure that these artifacts describe the same objects. Treating the release as a data product, we audit HuggingBench (SIGIR 2025), a benchmark for recommending Hugging Face resources, through data validation, a replication of its eleven recommendation methods and controlled experiments with three training seeds. In three of its four external KGs, the files pass key and range checks but violate the item-entity ident

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Minimal Superior Penalties: Characterising and Calibrating Decision-Aware Proper Scoring Rules
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03734v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training a classifier means letting a validation metric decide which model is kept and when training stops. A natural requirement on that metric is superiority: every correctly classified forecast should score better than every incorrectly classified one, however close the underlying probabilities are. Neither the Brier score nor the logarithmic score satisfies this on its own. We show that superiority is governed by the separation between two endpoints -- the supremum of the score on correct predictions and the infimum on incorrect predictions

ArXiv cs.LG.title: SSPE: Robust Sequential Staypoint Extraction in Degraded Trajectory Data
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03737v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Extracting semantically meaningful staypoints from raw trajectory streams is a foundational prerequisite for mobility analytics. However, real-world trajectory data is frequently degraded by severe spatial noise and protracted temporal dropouts. Classic threshold-based extraction methods, such as the widely adopted sliding-window algorithm, are highly sensitive to these anomalies, routinely fracturing continuous stationary episodes into disjointed fragments. To overcome this limitation, we propose the Sequential Staypoint Extraction (SSPE) algor

ArXiv cs.LG.title: RATSIFT: Resolution-Adaptive Transformer for Solar Irradiance Forecasting and Temporal Downscaling
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03738v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate forecasting and temporal downscaling of solar irradiance is critical for reliable renewable energy integration and grid management. Traditional methods often struggle to capture rapid irradiance variability. In this work, we develop a Transformer-based architecture for simultaneous forecasting and temporal downscaling. The model takes input data at arbitrary resolutions and generates outputs at any resolutions represented within the training data, leveraging both global and local contextual information. ArXiv cs.LG.title: CaRe-KT: Continuity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Knowledge Tracing
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03744v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge tracing (KT) estimates learners' evolving knowledge states from interaction histories to support adaptive learning. Retrieval-augmented KT improves these estimates using cross-learner behavioral evidence, but existing approaches typically separate evidence retrieval from downstream prediction. This creates a retrieval-inference alignment gap because evidence relevance varies with the learner's evolving state and prediction context. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Honest Small Decision Models for Finance: Scale, Specialization Collapse, and Mixed-Corpus Remediation
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03755v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Financial workflows need fast, calibrated, auditable decisions, not just generated text. We train System-1 decision models, small language models fine-tuned to answer typed questions (choice/score/noul) with a probability in a single forward pass, across two model families (K2-Horizon and Qwen3.5/3.8) and nine rungs from 0.8B to 32B parameters, using one frozen LoRA recipe on a public decision benchmark and two new finance corpora: a programmatic-gold policy corpus (rule-reading with exact labels) and a reality-labeled outcome corpus (19,640 rea

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Language Models Can Benefit from Domain-Specific Inductive Biases
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03756v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are typically trained with a single choice of architecture on diverse domains and data sources. Modern transformers have been extensively refined for such general-purpose learning, but are they equally effective across different subsets of the pretraining data? We investigate this question by training small language models from scratch on representative subsets of pretraining data such as web text, code, and mathematics. ArXiv cs.LG.title: The role of injected noise in diffusion model generalization
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03764v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion models trained on distinct datasets can produce highly similar samples when prompted with the same noise input, suggesting that they learn a generalized data distribution. We investigate the role of noise injected during the sampling process, and show that it plays an important role in making or breaking this strong generalization effect. I'll tell you what I tell them: If I knew that, I would make a life-changing bet on the market, levered up as far as I could, and then, after I made my money, […]

The Verge AI.title: Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
The Verge AI.description: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham have a distinctive feature in common: They're both famously bald, and that definitely hasn't changed in the last few days. However, there are some images of the two men circulating around X, Threads, and Bluesky in which they both have substantially more hair than their usual shaved […]

The Verge AI.title: Apple starts giving Siri AI access to third-party apps
The Verge AI.description: Apple will now let Siri AI perform actions across third-party apps. As part of the iOS 27.3 update rolling out on Tuesday, Apple announced developers can now integrate Siri AI's new features in "all apps," allowing the voice assistant to draw on a user's personal context, process natural language prompts, and use on-screen awareness to […]

The Verge AI.title: Apple’s latest watchOS beta includes its new always-on Audio Intelligence features
The Verge AI.description: Starting today, Siri can tune into the Apple Watch's mic with Audio Intelligence features that are available in the new watchOS 27.3 developer beta rolling out now. The two new additions are Siri Recap, which uses "ambient listening" to generate summaries of your conversation, and Live Rewind, which generates text transcripts of the last 15 […]

The Verge AI.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
The Verge AI.description: In many circles, "Ask Chat" has replaced "Google it," and that's reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google. Adam Fry, OpenAI's consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said […]

The Verge AI.title: Indie games are missing launch dates because Steam is backed up
The Verge AI.description: Many indie game developers have recently posted on social media about unexpectedly long approval wait times for their game submissions on Steam, with some of the approvals causing developers to miss their planned launch dates. For example, Studio Daimon, the team behind an upcoming title called Food Devils, had planned to launch the game in […]

The Verge AI.title: Netflix will show you themed recommendations through a new ‘AI Discover’ tab
The Verge AI.description: Netflix's TV app is getting a new "AI Discover" tab where the company will show experimental, AI-powered features to help you find new shows and movies to watch. The first of these experiments surfaces content based around themes, like "Something Light," "Family Movie Night," or "Quick Watches." When you pick a theme, Netflix will show […]

The Verge AI.title: Google is entirely disabling Search in schools that don’t want AI
The Verge AI.description: Google is completely turning off Search in schools that reject its AI features, the company told The New York Times. The decision was also shared in a broader education-related update from Google on Tuesday, saying that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search "will be entirely off" for K-12 student accounts […]

The Verge AI.title: Midterm elections 2026: all the news
The Verge AI.description: The 2026 midterm elections will determine the scope of President Donald Trump’s power in his final two years in office, and signal what voters care about going into the 2028 presidential election. While this year’s races are expected to be most broadly defined by affordability issues, there are several topics impacting the tech industry that […]

Wired AI.title: Here’s Why You Shouldn’t Use AI to Vote
Wired AI.description: From hallucinations to partisan bias, artificial intelligence chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude are not helpful when it comes to Election Day.

Wired AI.title: ‘Our Risk, Their Reward’: Zohran Mamdani on AI and Data Centers
Wired AI.description: Ahead of the midterms, WIRED talked to New York City’s mayor about data centers, AI in schools, and the future of the Democratic party.

Wired AI.title: When You Should—and Shouldn’t—Use AI to Search the Web
Wired AI.description: Chatbots are often quite good at retrieving the information you want from the web. But sometimes you’ll get better results by typing your query into a good old search engine.

Wired AI.title: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
Wired AI.description: WIRED uncovered some 400 apps and websites linked to Chinese-language developers that look like regular AI tools but had secret features that let users create violent AI-generated images and video.

Wired AI.title: Chatbots Are Leading Hikers Astray, With Dangerous Consequences
Wired AI.description: Outsourcing planning to AI can lead people to surrender their own critical thinking, which can have potentially deadly results in places like the backcountry.

Wired AI.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
Wired AI.description: Named Volta-Autodoxer, the recently uncovered malware uses AI tools to collect troves of data about victims, from login credentials and credit card numbers to Discord sessions and UberEats receipts.

Wired AI.title: Meta’s Muse Could Upend All Kinds of Businesses. It Hasn’t Yet
Wired AI.description: Companies have spent the past several weeks trying to reassure investors that Muse and other AI agents pose more of an opportunity than a threat.

Wired AI.title: An AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse’s Brain
Wired AI.description: A biotech startup let an agent choose a gene therapy and successfully inject the treatment, offering a startling glimpse of the future of research labs.

Wired AI.title: How a Contractor’s Claude Agent Got Into the Pentagon
Wired AI.description: This week on Uncanny Valley, we also discuss Anthropic’s IPO filing and the volunteers gearing up to counter ICE at the midterms.

Wired AI.title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
Wired AI.description: Sources tell WIRED that an Accenture employee’s personal Claude agent ran on a DOD network for two months before it was identified and the vulnerability could be patched.

MIT News — AI.title: Building connections across the research infrastructure
MIT News — AI.description: MIT.nano and the Northeast Microelectronics Coalition gathered facility leaders and technology professionals from across the nation to explore ways to make shared-access facilities more connected.

MIT News — AI.title: Powering up for a pivotal moment
MIT News — AI.description: From a nuclear revival to qubits, the MIT Energy Initiative’s annual research conference tracked deployment of today’s technologies to discovery of tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

MIT News — AI.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
MIT News — AI.description: The MIT professors collaborated to identify the first AI-discovered antibiotic, a scientific breakthrough that is widely recognized as a milestone in AI-driven drug discovery.

MIT News — AI.title: MIT affiliates named 2026 Schmidt Sciences AI2050 Fellows
MIT News — AI.description: Five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni are honored with fellowships to advance research on beneficial AI.

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
MIT News — AI.description: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata discuss a new project to track how AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

MIT News — AI.title: 3 Questions: Why infrastructure is entering a defining era
MIT News — AI.description: Professor Ali Jadbabaie describes how AI, digital transformation, climate change, and complex geopolitics are forcing engineers and policymakers to rethink how infrastructure is designed, built, and managed.

MIT News — AI.title: Making machines that can listen
MIT News — AI.description: Professor Paris Smaragdis develops computers with superhuman hearing for applications like speech recognition, music understanding, and environmental monitoring.

MIT News — AI.title: Learner collaborates with MIT peers to develop book of AI insights
MIT News — AI.description: Prabha Jha used her experience with MIT Open Learning’s program for senior executives to develop AI solutions for her employer, Verizon, and to write a book.

MIT News — AI.title: At New York Climate Week 2026, MIT connects with a global network
MIT News — AI.description: A cross-section of the MIT community convened discussions on topics ranging from data centers and super pollutants to agriculture and education.

MIT News — AI.title: At MIT, Martha Minow speaks on sustaining democracy, both by using and overcoming AI
MIT News — AI.description: In Compton Lecture, the distinguished legal scholar warns of potential “loss of the Enlightenment” while suggesting ways innovations can meet our civic and cultural needs.

MIT News — AI.title: Reinforcing the value of human understanding at MIT
MIT News — AI.description: During the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences’ 75th Anniversary Symposium, President Sally Kornbluth said “MIT has never needed your particular insight and guidance more than we do now.”

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the “messy” human mind
MIT News — AI.description: Assistant Professor Benjamin Lindquist studies how engineers deliberately injected randomness into early AI, giving rise to deep-learning models that sometimes hallucinate.

MIT News — AI.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices
MIT News — AI.description: “X-Hinges” helps design and 3D print items like lamps and gloves with an interactive twist: automatically embedded sensors that perceive and adaptively respond to human contact.

MIT News — AI.title: Why teaching AI about symmetry could make prenatal diagnosis more reliable
MIT News — AI.description: A model developed by researchers at MIT and Boston Children's Hospital adjusts scans on the fly to track fetal movement, potentially sparing families repeat hospital visits.

MIT News — AI.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world
MIT News — AI.description: New research can help AI models understand crystalline materials in 3D and reason about their properties.
